thread.title: Apple Buybacks May Total $21 Billion in Q2

author: Lawrence C. Strauss
title: Apple Buybacks May Total $21 Billion in Q2
text:
By Lawrence C. Strauss Aug. 1, 2018 4:58 p.m. ET As of late July, S&P 500 companies had repurchased $107.4 billion of their stock during the second quarter. Apple (AAPL) alone accounted for about $20 billion, or 20%, of that amount.
That percentage will drop as more companies announce second-quarter buybacks.
Howard Silverblatt , senior index analyst at S&P Dow Jones Indices , points out that Apple’s market cap is just less than 4% of the S&P 500’s.
Silverblatt estimates that Apple repurchased $20.7 billion of its stock in the second quarter, but that number is not final. Whatever it comes to, it’s very big.
It ranks as the second-highest quarterly buyback among S&P 500 companies ever. The largest one, also by Apple, totaled $22.8 billion in this year’s first quarter . In fact, of the top 20 S&P 500 quarterly stock repurchases, half of those were made by Apple.
Investors can expect more large buybacks from the technology giant. Of the $20 billion of stock that Apple bought back in the second quarter, $10 billion was tied to the company’s previous $210 repurchase program. The other $10 billion was part of a new authorization to buy back another $100 billion of stock.
